content.value_statement: Rising frequency and falling performance can hide different campaign problems. This skill compares trends and recommends rotating creative, widening audiences, or holding.
actual_capabilities: Compares current frequency, CTR, CVR, and reach with an early-flight baseline.
Distinguishes creative fatigue from audience saturation using trend behavior.
Returns one rotate, widen, or hold recommendation for each ad set.
Names the threshold and evidence supporting each recommendation.
Flags unreliable conversion data before using CVR in a decision.
Produces a reusable fatigue summary after the user approves saving.
limitations: Requires time-series data and cannot diagnose fatigue from one daily snapshot.
Cannot evaluate ad sets that remain in the platform learning phase.
Does not create replacement advertisements or calculate an account quality score.
Audience saturation may remain estimated when audience-size data is unavailable.

use_cases.title: Review Scaling Campaigns
use_cases.description: Compare ad-set trends and identify whether performance decay requires creative rotation, audience expansion, or no change.

use_cases.title: Validate Conversion Declines
use_cases.description: Check whether lower CVR reflects saturation or unreliable tracking before campaign changes are approved.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Client Actions
use_cases.description: Create consistent fatigue decisions across several client ad sets using named thresholds and evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Check One Ad Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this ad-set time series for fatigue. Recommend rotate, widen, or hold, and explain the evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner has one complete daily export.

prompt_templates.title: Compare With Baseline
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the first stable post-learning period as baseline. Compare frequency, reach, CTR, and CVR trends for this ad set.
prompt_templates.scenario: A manager needs a baseline-based diagnosis.

prompt_templates.title: Separate Fatigue and Saturation
prompt_templates.prompt: Determine whether creative fatigue, audience saturation, or both explain these trends. Name the dominant cause and one recommended action.
prompt_templates.scenario: A campaign shows mixed performance signals.

prompt_templates.title: Review Multiple Ad Sets
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate each ad set independently. Apply objective-specific frequency ceilings, flag measurement risks, and return one action with its threshold.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user is reviewing a scaled campaign.

output_examples.input: Prospecting frequency rose from 1.4 to 5.8 while CTR fell 42 percent and reach still grew.
output_examples.output: Creative fatigue is dominant. Rotate creative because CTR declined while frequency increased and reach continued growing.

output_examples.input: Retargeting reach plateaued, frequency reached 8.1, and both CTR and CVR declined.
output_examples.output: Audience saturation is dominant. Widen the audience because reach stalled while repeated exposure and performance decay increased.

output_examples.input: Frequency increased slightly, but CTR and CVR remained within normal variation.
output_examples.output: Hold. Current decay does not cross a supported threshold, so continue monitoring the time series.

best_practices: Provide daily or weekly exports covering the stable baseline and current period.
Include reach, frequency, CTR, CVR, spend, and learning-exit date when available.
Verify conversion trends against analytics or order records before acting on CVR decay.
anti_patterns: Do not request a fatigue diagnosis from a single-day dashboard snapshot.
Do not apply one universal frequency ceiling across objectives and audience types.
Do not treat estimated audience saturation or unverified CVR as measured evidence.

faq.question: What data does this skill need?
faq.answer: Provide a time series with frequency, reach, CTR, CVR, spend, and the learning-exit date when available.

faq.question: Can it analyze one daily snapshot?
faq.answer: No. It needs multiple periods to compare performance slopes with a stable baseline.

faq.question: How does it identify creative fatigue?
faq.answer: Creative fatigue is indicated when CTR declines and frequency rises while reach continues growing.

faq.question: How does it identify audience saturation?
faq.answer: Saturation is indicated when reach plateaus while frequency climbs and CTR or CVR declines.

faq.question: Does it create replacement ads?
faq.answer: No. It diagnoses the problem and can route a rotation decision to a creative-building skill.

faq.question: Can it use data without CVR?
faq.answer: Yes. It can assess a creative-fatigue signal from CTR and frequency, while clearly marking CVR as unavailable.
